free_tier.stated: Scales 250 GB → 5 PB per bucket, 10 billion objects, 20K RPS. Entry plan $5/mo = 250 GB + 1 TB outbound included.

egress.terms: 1 TB/month outbound included with the base plan (shared with the account's Linode transfer pool), then $0.005/GB = $5/TB. Inbound free.

tooling: S3 API, rclone s3 backend, any SDK. Cluster URL per region.
chaining: The 1 TB/month included egress is the free slice: enough for 33 GB/day, matching Gcore. Its real use is as a *stable S3 origin* behind one of the free CDNs, not as the delivery path — $5/TB egress is good but Bunny's Volume tier matches it and CacheFly/Telnyx beat it.
limits_note: per-object-cap: none published. $20/TB/mo storage is the weak number (vs $6 Telnyx, $10 Bunny, $2 Hetzner) — you are paying for Akamai's network, not for bytes.
reliability_note: Post-Linode acquisition; the linode.com pagess now redirect to akamai.com. Excellent durability, irrelevant price.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: → resolves to https://www.akamai.com/products/object-storage: 'Scale from 250 GB to 5 PB per bucket', 'up to 20K RPS', 'free inbound transfer and up to 1TB outbound is included'
cross-checked against third-party catalogues (dracon.uk, s3providers.com): $20.00/TB·mo storage, $5.00/TB egress — medium confidence because I could not read the raw rate card itself
